trace.reasoning: The patient is a 12-year-old girl with a tender, palpable mass below the left knee and preserved joint range of motion. While the provided text lacks specific imaging details like "ground-glass" matrix or "soap bubble" appearance, the clinical presentation of a benign-appearing, slow-growing tibial lesion in a child strongly favors Non-ossifying fibroma. Osteofibrous dysplasia and Adamantinoma are less likely due to age and typical radiographic features not described. Low-grade chondrosarcoma is rare in this age group, and aneurysmal bone cysts usually present with more acute symptoms or expansile thinning. Non-ossifying fibroma is the most common benign bone tumor in children, fitting the asymptomatic nature and location best.
